dicas.texto: Ótima observação! Quando temos mais de um inteiro e uma fração, como representamos isso como uma única fração? Pense: quantos quartos há em dois inteiros?
Você está no caminho certo! Primeiro, transforme os 2 inteiros em quartos (lembre-se: 1 inteiro = 4/4). Depois some os 3/4 que sobraram.
Quase lá! Se cada copo tem 4 partes, então 2 copos inteiros têm 8 partes. Some mais 3 partes. Quantas partes no total?
Você está muito perto! 2 inteiros = 8/4. Agora some 8/4 + 3/4. Some só os numeradores — quanto dá?
Boa pergunta! Se a reta está dividida em quartos, como você localiza 11/4? Em quantos quartos cabe 1 inteiro?
Continue assim! Conte os quartos: 0, 1/4, 2/4, ..., até chegar em 11/4. Marque exatamente onde parar.
Quase lá! 11/4 está depois de 2 (que é 8/4). Conte: 9/4 (primeira marca após 2), 10/4 (segunda), 11/4 (terceira).
Você está quase! A partir do 2, avance 3 marcas pequenas (pois 11 – 8 = 3). Onde caiu o ponto?

solutionTrace.thinking: O problema descreve que foram usadas 2 xícaras cheias (uma para Lili e uma para sua irmã) e mais 3/4 de uma terceira xícara. Preciso somar essas quantidades para obter a fração total.

solutionTrace.action: Converter a soma em fração imprópria
solutionTrace.thinking: 2 inteiros equivalem a 8/4, então 8/4 + 3/4 = 11/4. Essa é a fração total de suco preparado.

solutionTrace.action: Inserir o numerador no campo f1
solutionTrace.thinking: Devo digitar 11 no campo superior da fração (f1).

solutionTrace.action: Inserir o denominador no campo f2
solutionTrace.thinking: Devo digitar 4 no campo inferior da fração (f2).
11/4 = 2,75. A reta vai de 0 a 3 com divisões em quartos (0, 1/4, 2/4, ..., 12/4). 11/4 está entre 2 (8/4) e 3 (12/4), exatamente na terceira marca após 2.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 4 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)
grupo com m1/m2/m3, exibido depois de Convert
botão "Convert": abre as caixas do número misto (m1, m2, m3) para reescrever a fração

passos.acao: Use the fraction model to represent two full cups and three-fourths of another cup.
Use the fraction model to rewrite the total amount as an improper fraction.
Manipulate the numerator field to identify the top number in the fraction.
Manipulate the denominator field to identify the bottom number in the fraction.
Enter the numerator of the fraction in field f1.
Enter the denominator of the fraction in field f2.
Mark the point for 11/4 on the number line from 0 to 3.
Use Convert to rewrite 11/4 as a mixed number in the rightFraction group.

dicas.texto: Separate the juice into the two completely filled cups and the remaining part of a cup.
Represent each complete cup as one whole, then show the remaining part using four equal sections.
Select two whole units and shade three of the four equal parts in the additional unit.
Combine the whole units with the shaded fractional part and record the amount as a mixed number.
An improper fraction represents the entire amount using equal fractional parts.
Multiply the whole-number part by the denominator, then add the numerator while keeping the denominator.
Use four equal parts for each whole unit and count all the fourths represented by the two wholes and the remaining part.
Find the total number of fourths, place that count above the unchanged denominator, and enter the resulting fraction.
Look at the position of each number relative to the fraction bar.
The numerator tells how many equal parts are counted in the fraction.
Focus on the number written above the slash in the improper fraction.
Select the upper number of the fraction and enter that whole-number value in the numerator field.
The denominator describes the number of equal parts in one whole.
Find the number below the fraction bar and use it as the denominator.
The fraction is divided into fourths, so focus on the lower number.
Select the lower number of the fraction and enter that whole-number value in the denominator field.
The upper field corresponds to the numerator.
Read the improper fraction from top to bottom and place its upper value in f1.
Use the total count of fourths for the upper field rather than the number of parts in one whole.
Type the numerator value into f1, the numeric field above the fraction bar.
The lower field tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Place the denominator below the fraction bar in the lower numeric field.
The amount is measured in fourths, so the denominator identifies four equal parts.
Type the denominator value into f2, the numeric field below the fraction bar.
First determine which two consecutive whole numbers contain the fraction.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to locate the value on the number line.
Eleven fourths is two whole units and three of the four equal parts after 2.
On the interval from 2 to 3, move to the third of the four equal subdivisions and place the point there.
An improper fraction can be separated into whole groups and a remaining fractional part.
Divide the numerator by the denominator; the quotient is the whole part and the remainder becomes the new numerator.
Four fits into eleven two complete times, with three parts left over.
Enter the quotient as m1, the remainder as m2, and keep the original denominator as m3 after selecting Convert.

exercicio.statement:
Every morning, Lili's mother prepares a pitcher of tomato juice for Lili and her sister. One morning, Lili's mother made the pitcher a bit too large; it completely filled Lili's cup, her sister's up, and the left over filled about 3/4 of a third cup. Show the number of cups of tomato juice Lili's mother prepared that morning on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?
